title: Eight ways apps put a file beside a conversation
sub: From 30 iPad, desktop and web apps plus Apple’s guidelines (Oct 23). Most chat-plus-file apps now split the window and give the file the wider side. Full notes: .claude/design/ipad-artifact-split/research.md

patterns.name: Replace the view
patterns.what: Tapping a file swaps the chat for the file, as a sheet or a full-screen viewer. The transcript is gone until you close it.
patterns.seen: lfg today, Mail and Slack on iPad, Quick Look
patterns.lfg: What we replace on wide windows. It stays as the fallback in portrait and narrow windows.

patterns.name: File beside the chat
patterns.what: The chat shrinks to a column and keeps working. The file gets the wider side, and a handle resizes the split.
patterns.seen: Claude web (about 50/50), Gemini (36/64), ChatGPT Codex (26/74), Swift Playgrounds
patterns.lfg: Option A. About 40/60: the transcript is built for phone width, and the file is what needs room.

patterns.name: The list steps aside
patterns.what: If there is no room, the sidebar collapses when the file opens and comes back as an overlay. Closing the file puts it back.
patterns.seen: Claude and Gemini (icon rail), Mail on iPad. Apple (WWDC25): layout changes must undo themselves.
patterns.lfg: Taken, by width: the list hides on the 11-inch and stays on the 13-inch.

patterns.name: Inspector column
patterns.what: A fixed, narrow column at the trailing edge (Apple’s example: 225 to 400pt), next to the list.
patterns.seen: Keynote, Xcode, Preview, SwiftUI .inspector. Also the Claude iPad app’s one-third-width artifact pane.
patterns.lfg: Option B. It is too narrow for web pages and documents. Users complain most about the Claude iPad pane for this reason (issue #100553).

patterns.name: Full-width toggle
patterns.what: One button sends the file to full width. The same button brings back the exact split.
patterns.seen: Swift Playgrounds (Expand / Contract Canvas), Claude, Final Cut Pro. Users ask for it in Codex.
patterns.lfg: Taken. Expand is in the pane header, and a chip with the session’s status brings the transcript back.

patterns.name: Show where it came from
patterns.what: The source card stays tinted while its file is open, and the viewer can jump back to that message.
patterns.seen: Gemini (tinted card), Skype’s media gallery. Apple: persistently highlight the current selection.
patterns.lfg: Taken. The card turns blue and says Open, and ••• has Show in transcript. A live transcript never scrolls by itself.

patterns.name: Peek overlay
patterns.what: A panel slides over the content for a quick look and closes with one tap.
patterns.seen: Notion side peek, Linear peek, Quick Look
patterns.lfg: Not taken: it covers a transcript that is still moving.

patterns.name: Tabs and split editors
patterns.what: Several files in tabs and groups that you open, arrange and close yourself.
patterns.seen: VS Code, Cursor, Claude Design, GoodNotes
patterns.lfg: Not taken: the session already defines its files. One pane replaces its file on each tap, with the Files list and a media strip.
